headline: SELKIRK COPPER MINTO PEA: C$494M NPV, 47.8% IRR, 1.9-YEAR PAYBACK — YUKON BROWNFIELD 2.7X RETURNS ON C$186M BUILD
snippet: Selkirk Copper Mines released a positive preliminary economic assessment for the Minto Project in the Yukon on September 25, 2026, outlining a C$494 million after-tax NPV at a 7% discount rate and 47.8% IRR — approximately 2.7 times the C$186 million initial capital estimate, with a 1.9-year payback on a 13-year mine life. The economic study assumed conservative planning prices of US$5.00/lb copper, US$3,600/oz gold and US$50/oz silver — all materially below current spot — suggesting significant upside leverage at prevailing market prices. A Phase 2 drilling programme of 50,000 metres is nearing completion; its results were excluded from the PEA but will feed a feasibility study targeted for Q4 2026. Minto is one of the few permitted, infrastructure-equipped brownfield copper-gold-silver operations in Canadian territory, a category of asset that attracts acute institutional buy-out interest in a world where new copper mine permitting takes 15-20 years. For junior copper investors, the Minto PEA sets a concrete valuation benchmark for Yukon copper-gold brownfield projects.

headline: KINROSS GOLD -10% ON LA COIPA PRODUCTION CUT — 8% GUIDANCE SLASH; AISC JUMPS TO $1,900; ROUND MOUNTAIN ALSO MISSES
snippet: Kinross Gold (TSX/NYSE: KGC) shares fell more than 10% after the producer slashed its 2026 and 2027 production outlook by approximately 8% from prior guidance midpoints, citing winter storm disruptions and higher-than-expected copper grades causing poor gold and silver recoveries at La Coipa in Chile, compounded by weaker mining rates at Round Mountain in Nevada. New guidance of 1.84-1.86 million gold-equivalent ounces per year replaces the prior 1.9-2.1 million range, while all-in sustaining costs climb to US$1,850-1,900 per ounce from $1,730. Kinross simultaneously boosted its shareholder payout programme, which limited the market reaction but could not prevent the largest single-session decline for the stock in 2026. The La Coipa operational miss, driven by Chilean winter weather and sulphide ore metallurgy problems, illustrates that even well-capitalised senior producers face mine-specific variance at record gold prices — reinforcing the case for royalty and streaming exposure alongside direct equity positions for retail investors managing senior producer risk.

headline: VIKING MINES (VKA) +25%: 5 CONSECUTIVE TUNGSTEN HITS AT LINKA NEVADA — 18m AT 0.42% WO3; CRITICAL MINERAL IN US JURISDICTION
snippet: Viking Mines (ASX: VKA) surged 25% on September 24 after RC drilling below the historic Linka Mine in Nevada returned five consecutive holes with significant tungsten mineralisation, including highlight intercepts of 18 metres at 0.42% WO3 and 13 metres at 0.46% WO3 — grades consistent with the mine's active 1950s operational period and indicating ore zone continuity to depth. Seven further holes are pending assay with results expected mid-October, including LKRC0016 and LKRC0017 which have already logged 9.9m and 12.2m of visible scheelite under UV light respectively. Tungsten is classified as a critical mineral by the US and EU for irreplaceable use in cutting tools and armour-piercing applications; Nevada jurisdiction adds strategic domestic-supply appeal. The stock moved higher on a day when the broader ASX fell, a divergence that typically signals institutional rather than retail-driven accumulation. For junior mining investors, the five-consecutive-hole intercept pattern removes the single-hole discovery risk that often caps first-result moves.

headline: LITCHFIELD MINERALS +12.5%: 68m AT 0.62% CU FROM 2m DEPTH AT OONAGALABI NT — NEAR-SURFACE CU-ZN-AG OPENS LOW-CAPEX MINE CASE
snippet: Litchfield Minerals (ASX: LMS) gained 12.5% on September 24 after Phase 3 drilling at Oonagalabi in the Northern Territory returned a 68.26-metre interval grading 0.62% copper, 1.44% zinc and 4.3 g/t silver starting from just 2 metres depth — confirming both the lateral scale and highly accessible geometry of the copper-zinc-silver system. A southwest intercept also beginning near-surface expands the deposit's footprint. Near-surface polymetallic mineralisation reduces pre-stripping requirements and supports lower-capex open-cut mine designs, a meaningful economic differentiator for junior copper projects at a time when capital intensity is the primary gating factor for mid-tier acquisition interest. LMS moved higher alongside Viking Mines (VKA) on the same ASX session, an unusual co-event suggesting broad institutional activity in the critical minerals junior space on September 24.

headline: VIZSLA COPPER STAKES MILLER PORPHYRY ADJACENT TO MT. MILLIGAN BC — 25,274 HA; MAG-TEL SURVEY STARTS IMMEDIATELY
snippet: Vizsla Copper (TSX: VCU) announced the staking of the Miller copper-gold porphyry project in central British Columbia, approximately 145 kilometres north of Prince George — a 25,274-hectare land package adjacent to Centerra Gold's operating Mount Milligan mine, one of British Columbia's largest copper-gold operations. Magnetotelluric surveying is scheduled to begin immediately. The Miller acquisition expands Vizsla's BC portfolio beyond its flagship Poplar copper porphyry system and increases exposure to the most prolific copper-gold porphyry belt in North America at a time when tier-1 copper porphyry discoveries command the highest institutional premiums in the junior sector. Adjacency to Mount Milligan provides existing infrastructure optionality and known geological context for the acquired ground, reducing the cost and risk of the initial exploration programme relative to a greenfield staking in an unknown district.

headline: CAPRICORN METALS KARLAWINDA DELIVERED ON-TIME AT 6.5 MTPA — WA GOLD MINE TARGETING 150,000 OZ/YR; 12-MONTH BUILD COMPLETE
snippet: Capricorn Metals (ASX: CMM) completed construction of the Karlawinda Expansion Project in Western Australia on schedule in late September 2026, achieving steady-state throughput of 6.5 million tonnes per annum through new parallel crushing, milling and CIL circuits and targeting approximately 150,000 ounces of gold per year going forward. The expansion was delivered in 12 months from start to commissioning completion. At current gold prices above USD 4,280/oz, a 150,000-oz-per-year low-cost Western Australian operation generates substantial annual free cash flow at Capricorn's AISC profile, sufficient to fund further organic growth without equity dilution. The on-time, on-budget delivery distinguishes Capricorn as an operator in an environment where many Australian mine expansions are suffering cost overruns and labour shortages. The completion is expected to drive meaningful earnings upgrades and increased institutional coverage.

headline: CATL JIANXIAWO MINE EIA STAYS REVOKED — BENCHMARK FLIPS 2027 LITHIUM TO DEFICIT; 2026 SUPPLY FORECAST CUT 49%
snippet: China's largest-capacity lithium mine, CATL's Jianxiawo operation in Sichuan, remains on care and maintenance after regulators revoked its environmental approval for the second time, following a brief July 2026 informal restart that bypassed an unresolved tailings pond dispute and drew over 70 regulatory complaints. Benchmark Mineral Intelligence cut its 2026 mined output forecast for Jianxiawo to 32,000 tonnes of LCE from 62,500 tonnes — a 49% reduction — and flipped its 2027 global lithium market balance from surplus to deficit. The mine accounts for approximately 4% of global lithium supply; the sustained outage, combined with guidance cuts from Albemarle and Pilbara Minerals, is compressing supply at a moment when battery energy storage demand is tracking above the EV-only forecast models that underpinned prior surplus projections. For junior lithium companies on the ASX and TSXV, an emerging structural 2027 deficit represents the first constructive macro backdrop for project valuations since 2022.

headline: GLENCORE + NTH CYCLE SEAL 24,000T/YR BATTERY RECYCLING DEAL — ELECTROCHEMICAL LITHIUM + NICKEL RECOVERY AT COMMERCIAL SCALE
snippet: Glencore and Nth Cycle announced an agreement under which Glencore will supply Nth Cycle with approximately 24,000 metric tonnes per year of shredded battery material from end-of-life EV and consumer electronics batteries, with Nth Cycle applying its electrochemical separation technology to recover lithium, nickel and other battery metals. The September 25 disclosure, part of the CIM's weekly mining recap, represents one of the largest commercial-scale commitments to battery recycling built around an electrochemical rather than a smelter-based pathway. The commercial deployment of direct battery recycling begins to establish a recycled-metal cost curve that competes with primary lithium and nickel mine supply — a structural headwind for long-dated greenfield projects that must model their economics against falling recycled-material recovery costs as EV fleet retirement volumes scale through the 2030s. The deal signals Glencore's strategic intent to participate in the battery materials loop beyond primary mining.

headline: GOLD MINERS ENTERING 'EXPLOSIVE NEW PHASE' ABOVE $4,300 — FREE CASH FLOW SIGNALS RE-RATING; ACQUISITION CYCLE ACCELERATING
snippet: A September 24 analysis argues that gold mining companies are entering a potentially explosive new phase at current prices above $4,300 per ounce, with producer free cash flow margins running 40-50% above the five-year average and creating balance-sheet firepower for acquisition activity that historically precedes junior re-ratings. The analyst draws parallels to the 2007-2008 and 2010-2011 phases when major producers began aggressively acquiring exploration-stage assets after establishing multi-year sustained high gold prices. The analysis argues the current cycle — seniors re-rating first, now bidding for mid-tiers, junior acquisitions next — is playing out faster than prior cycles given tighter exploration pipelines and the scarcity of new discovery-stage projects in Tier 1 jurisdictions. The Kinross Gold production miss announced the same week reinforces the argument: when organic production growth stalls at record prices, acquisition becomes the primary growth lever for senior producers, compressing the M&A discount applied to quality junior assets.

headline: COT SEPT 25: MANAGED MONEY GOLD PACE AT 97TH PERCENTILE — COMMERCIAL SHORTS NEAR EXTREME; ECHOES 2018 AND 2022 PRE-PIVOT
snippet: The September 25 Commitments of Traders analysis from GoldSeek covers COMEX positions through the September 22 cutoff and shows managed money net longs in gold at the 70th percentile of the historical range, with the pace of position building over the prior eight weeks registering at the 97th percentile — a configuration that historically signals deep institutional commitment to the gold trade rather than retail crowding. Commercial traders hold short positions near a historic absolute extreme. USDX positioning remains elevated, consistent with the dollar's role as the near-term headwind. Silver COT shows managed money positioned more conservatively relative to the January peak than gold, a relative dynamic that historically resolves in silver's favour once rate-hike expectations peak. The extreme commercial short position in gold combined with the elevated managed money building pace matches patterns from the 2018-2019 and 2022-2023 pre-pivot environments — both of which resolved sharply when rate expectations shifted — making the current setup a closely watched technical signal for gold price direction in Q4 2026.

headline: GOLD STRIKE RESOURCES FLORIN GOLD YUKON 2026 DRILL PROGRAM WRAPS — SAMPLES SHIPPED; ASSAYS DUE MID-OCTOBER
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Gold Strike Resources
snippet: Gold Strike Resources Corp. (TSXV: GSR) announced September 24 that its 2026 drill programme at the Florin Gold Project in the Yukon is complete, with over 50% of all samples already collected and shipped to the laboratory and assay results expected in mid-October 2026. Florin sits in the Dawson Range gold belt, a Yukon district that has attracted stepped-up institutional attention following recent results in the region. The mid-October result window places GSR among the identifiable Q4 catalyst names on the TSXV — a key benefit of the industry-wide 75-day assay queue bottleneck, which compresses drill-result news flow into predictable windows that investors with a watchlist advantage can position ahead of. For retail investors tracking multiple TSXV juniors, a completed drill programme with a known sample-to-lab timeline creates a specific date range for due diligence rather than an open-ended wait.

headline: MX EXPLORATION: CAD 194M GOLD MINE SELF-FUNDED BY BULK SAMPLE — NO EQUITY DILUTION IF 12 G/T RESOURCE HOLDS AT ABITIBI
snippet: A September 2026 analysis of MX Exploration's Abitibi gold project examines the company's strategy of funding a CAD 194 million Phase One mine through a CAD 60 million bulk sample programme targeting 25,000 ounces of pre-commercial production — replacing a traditional equity raise if the 12 g/t average grade holds against bulk-sample tonnage. At September 2026 gold prices approximately 7% above the USD 4,000/oz planning assumption, the financial margin between the projected funding stack and the CAD 194 million capex target has widened in the company's favour. The analysis identifies grade reconciliation as the single most consequential risk variable, with the 20,000-28,000 ounce yield range representing a 32% spread around the base case. Six drill rigs are active across the 570-square-kilometre Abitibi package. If the self-funding model executes, it would represent one of the most capital-efficient junior mine developments in recent Abitibi history and a potential template for other high-grade open-pittable juniors operating in the current high-gold-price environment where traditional equity raises are viewed as increasingly dilutive.
